input.question: Why do taste testers use gold cutlery?
input.ground_truth: Gold is one of the least reactive substances in the world. As a result when your job is tasting extremely subtle things that neutrality is vital. More reactive things like plastic, steel, or silver have a chance of altering the flavor of the food for them. While you and I may not have sophisticated enough tastes to tell the difference they can, and that can affect their job performances.

Okay! Imagine you want to taste a tiny bit of ice cream. You wouldn’t use a plastic spoon because it might make the ice cream taste funny or change the way it feels in your mouth. 

Gold cutlery is super clean and doesn’t react with food. It doesn’t have any taste by itself, so when taste testers use it, they know they are only tasting the food, not the spoon. Also, gold is very shiny and pretty, which makes people think it’s special and clean. 

So, taste testers use gold cutlery to make sure they get the *real* taste of the food, just like you want to taste your ice cream, not the spoon!
